diagnosis.scope: Posthoc descriptions of recorded worlds only. Torque errors concern active joints. Predictions use prepared velocity; observed actuator force evolves during the held interval and is not measured contact reaction. Release motion is sampled at controller observations. No counterfactual trajectories, causal isolation or new eligibility decisions.

interpretation: This is one exposed full-route body with ten moment controllers. Do not extrapolate its mechanisms to every broad-search body or isolate one factor causally.

Nineteen of twenty-four completed neutral-release intervals lose rotation. Six lose 9.96 to 10.61 degrees in 0.2 seconds; five tiny positive intervals belong to the clock profile with no distal contact.

The three continuous variants plateau near 11.5 degrees, versus a 23.48-degree peak for the fresh selected reference. Their retained target postures differ; these trajectories do not isolate steering from posture and guard effects.

Active-joint mean torque error increases after joint protection. Native actuator-force error against the prepared request is similar, but neither is measured contact reaction or a certificate that another requested wrench can be realized.

Keep joint guards. Test retaining useful support while other limbs obtain contact instead of retracting every leg to neutral. Replacement-contact success, dynamic feasibility, actual recovery and learned adaptation remain unproved.
next_gate: Implement and prospectively compare support-preserving changeovers across the broad body cohort. Start from each useful exposed reference profile. Keep its ordinary behavior until measured progress stalls; retain existing support while selected unloaded limbs seek replacement contact, and permit release only after measured replacement contact. Keep original joint protection and a bounded fallback to the reference behavior. Factor limb choice, posture and transition conditions across many bodies, with fresh brake, timed and selected-reference comparators. A full route must cover preserved support, contact acquisition, changeover and no-replacement fallback before compact discovery. Five-degree improvement over the fresh selected reference, full retained-path screening and fresh varied-start confirmation remain required; this diagnosis establishes no recovery or alternative-action benefit.
